module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 197

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/197](https://www.erdosproblems.com/197)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Set

namespace Erdos197

/--
Can $\mathbb{N}$ be partitioned into two sets, each of which can be permuted to avoid monotone
3-term arithmetic progressions?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_197 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ A B : Set ℕ, IsCompl A B ∧
      (∃ f : ℕ ≃ A, ¬HasMonotoneAP (Subtype.val ∘ f) 3) ∧
      (∃ g : ℕ ≃ B, ¬HasMonotoneAP (Subtype.val ∘ g) 3) := by
  sorry

end Erdos197

reformulations.difference: The Lean asks for bijections `f : ℕ ≃ A` and `g : ℕ ≃ B`. This forces both parts to be infinite and arranged as ω-sequences. The source's wording, a partition into two sets each of which can be permuted, does not explicitly rule out a finite or empty part, which would be permuted as a finite sequence.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A finite part is never usable, because its complement is then cofinite, and every enumeration (b_i) of a set containing [N,∞) has a monotone 3-AP. Proof: let i0 be the first index with b_{i0} ≥ N. Let i1 be the first index after i0 with b_{i1} > b_{i0}. Then c = 2·b_{i1} − b_{i0} ≥ N lies in the set. It cannot sit before i0, since those values are < N. It cannot sit between i0 and i1, since those values are < b_{i0}. So (b_{i0}, b_{i1}, c) is an increasing 3-AP at increasing indices. An empty part fails the same way, since the other part is then all of ℕ. So any valid partition has two infinite parts, and for those, 'permuted' means exactly a bijection ℕ ≃ part. In Lean I proved `cofinite_hasMonotoneAP` (for B with Bᶜ finite, every g : ℕ ≃ B satisfies HasMonotoneAP (val ∘ g) 3). I also proved `allow_finite_parts_iff`: for an arbitrary predicate P on finite parts, the version where each part is either (finite ∧ P) or has a 3-AP-free enumeration ℕ ≃ part is ↔ the right-hand side of `erdos_197`. Everything is sorry-free (axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound).

reformulations.difference: Lean partitions ℕ = {0,1,2,...}. erdosproblems.com's ℕ and the literature (Adenwalla arXiv:2211.04451, following Davis–Entringer–Graham–Simmons and Erdős–Graham) use the positive integers {1,2,...}.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Translation n ↦ n+1 is a bijection {0,1,...} → {1,2,...}. It maps 3-term APs (x, x+d, x+2d) to 3-term APs and leaves the index order of an enumeration untouched, so it carries partitions with 3-AP-free enumerations both ways. Proved in Lean as `nat_iff_posint`: the right-hand side of `erdos_197` is ↔ the same statement for a disjoint pair A, B with A ∪ B = {n | 0 < n}. Sorry-free.

review.notes:
The file has one declaration, `Erdos197.erdos_197`. Its docstring reproduces erdosproblems.com/197 word for word: "Can ℕ be partitioned into two sets, each of which can be permuted to avoid monotone 3-term arithmetic progressions?" The site's only remark ("If three sets are allowed then this is possible") is not formalized. That omission is not a defect.

Semantics, checked in Lean:
- I proved `HasMonotoneAP f 3 ↔ ∃ i<j<k, ∃ a d, (f i, f j, f k) = (a, a+d, a+2d) ∨ (a+2d, a+d, a)` for f : ℕ → ℕ. So the predicate is exactly "some increasing or decreasing 3-term AP occurs at increasing positions". This matches Adenwalla's definition ("there does not exist an increasing or decreasing subsequence of the permutation that forms a k-term arithmetic progression") and the phrasing on erdosproblems.com/196.
- The difference d is a natural number, and the list-reversal disjunct covers decreasing APs. The case d = 0 is unreachable, because `Subtype.val ∘ f` is injective and the indices are strictly increasing.
- `IsCompl A B` is a genuine partition of ℕ.
- The right-hand side is the positive form of the question, so `answer(True)` would mean "yes". It is not a negated conjecture.
- `#check` shows `True ↔ …`. This is the repository's default `answer(sorry)` elaborator setting at `Prop` (alwaysTrue), not a defect of this file.
- Sanity check: I proved in Lean that no enumeration of ℕ avoids monotone 3-APs (the DEGS77 fact), so the easy candidates fail as expected.

The two formal differences from the source are recorded under reformulations with sorry-free proofs: both parts are forced infinite, and ℕ includes 0.

Status: the file says `research open`, and the source agrees. The erdosproblems.com snapshot of 2026-08-11 shows OPEN with no comments, and problems.yaml says open. Adenwalla's paper also lists the question as open.

Limitation: I could not read the original Erdős–Graham wording ([ErGr79], [ErGr80]). The available PDFs are image-only scans and no OCR tools were available. I relied on erdosproblems.com, the file's cited source, and on Adenwalla's restatement of the question, which cites [Davis77, ErGr80, Geneson18, LeSaulnier11]: "Is it possible to partition the positive integers into two sets, each of which can be permuted to avoid 3-APs?"

My scratch proofs are in /workspace/review/scratch2.lean. I made no changes under /opt/formal-conjectures. The pre-existing `lakefile.toml` modification and `run/` directory predate my session, and 197.lean and the AP definitions file are unchanged from the commit.
